steps.say: Next-token prediction scales because text comes from a discrete, fixed vocabulary. Audio doesn't.

steps.caption: waveform, tokens, waveform
steps.say: So turn the waveform into tokens, train on the tokens, and turn them back into sound.

scenes.headline: How LiquidCodec turns speech into tokens
scenes.sub: Liquid AI's codec behind LFM3-Audio and LFM3-Omni
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Fintan! A language model predicts integers. Speech is twenty-four thousand real numbers a second. A codec sits in between.

steps.say: Every neural codec has three parts. An encoder squeezes time into a few vectors a second.

steps.caption: encoder, quantiser, decoder
steps.say: A quantiser turns each vector into integers. A decoder turns integers back into sound.

steps.term: Codebook: a learned list of vectors
steps.say: The old way is residual quantisation. Codebook one picks the nearest vector.
Codebook two quantises what is left over, and so on, each correction smaller than the last.

scenes.title: Two ways to turn a vector into integers

legend: Each code fixes what the codes before it missed
Get code one wrong, and the rest miss too
Round each number to its own levels
Twelve groups, twelve tokens; one wrong code moves one axis

steps.say: Here is a toy in two dimensions. Each code is a correction to the codes before it, and the path closes in on the point.
Now let the model get code one slightly wrong. The later codes still describe the old leftover, so the whole path misses.
Grouped scalar quantisation throws the codebooks away. Each of four numbers is rounded to its own grid of levels.
Twelve groups make twelve tokens. A wrong code for one group moves one number by one step. The others are still right.
Liquid's own figure. Four numbers, with eight, seven, six and six levels.

steps.caption: 8 x 7 x 6 x 6 = 2,016 codes per group
steps.say: Together they pick one of two thousand and sixteen codes. Twelve groups, twelve tokens a frame.

scenes.title: What a second of speech costs

parts.note: frames a second, one every 80 ms
parts.say: Twelve and a half frames a second.

parts.note: 150 tokens a second for the language model
parts.say: Twelve codes a frame, so a hundred and fifty tokens a second.
About eleven bits each. Mimi with twelve codebooks lands on the same bitrate, which makes it a fair rival.

scenes.say: The bill is three numbers multiplied.

steps.term: STFT: the spectrum, frame by frame
steps.say: Inside, the encoder starts from a spectrum, seventy-five a second, stacks six into one, and runs an eight-block LFM3 stack.
The decoder runs the same stack, then predicts a spectrum and lets an inverse FFT make the samples. No learned upsampling at all.

scenes.title: Who wins, across eight test sets

states.say: On Liquid's eight test sets it has the best perceptual quality score and the lowest mel distance on every one.
The PESQ score goes the other way. NanoCodec wins seven of eight.
And in text to speech, its tokens give the lowest error rate on four sets of eight.

scenes.title: Same TTS model, four codecs: LibriSpeech WER
scenes.say: That is the better experiment: the same backbone, data and compute, only the codec changed. Mimi doubles the error rate.
